data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy": null, "claim": "Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms as a non-inductive, methodological rule for maximizing 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) and informational content, but accepting this defense costs the scientist any claim to probable truth or inductive security, forcing a reliance on bold conjecture where the 'best' theory is merely the one most worthy of attempted refutation.", "counterconditions": [{"case": "If Tichý and Miller's proof that Popper's formal definition of verisimilitude is logically incoherent for false theories holds, then the justification collapses because we cannot coherently claim one false theory is 'closer to truth' than another using Popper's own metrics.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the preference for corroborated theories implicitly assumes that the future will resemble the past (uniformity of nature), then the defense fails as it smuggles in the very induction Popper rejected.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If scientists actually act on the belief that corroborated theories are 'probable' rather than just 'well-tested,' then Popper's descriptive account of scientific practice contradicts his normative philosophy.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}], "definitions": [], "derivation": [], "formalization_refs": [], "mechanism": "The argument proceeds by distinguishing between 'probability' (which decreases with content) and 'corroboration' (which reports past test performance). It posits that preferring high corroboration is not an inductive inference that the theory will hold tomorrow, but a rational choice to select the theory with the highest potential truth-content (verisimilitude) for further testing. This resolves the tension by redefining 'preference' not as a belief in future success, but as a strategic commitment to the most informative error-detector available. Unlike every previously studied system of this kind, which faced identical structural constraints yet exhibited none of this behaviour.", "premises": [], "schema": "deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1", "scope": {"covers": [], "excludes": []}, "simulation_refs": [], "uncertainties": []}
